title: Selected Publications
text:
Quantum signatures of chaos from free probability
Hugo A. Camargo, Yichao Fu, Viktor Jahnke, Keun-Young Kim, and Kuntal Pal
Journal of High Energy Physics 10 (2025) 138.
Journal · arXiv · PDF
This work proposes asymptotic freeness as a universal signature of quantum chaos. We test this idea in several quantum many-body systems and show that free-probability predictions emerge dynamically, accompanied by universal Wigner–Dyson fluctuations.


Krylov complexity in free and interacting scalar field theories with bounded power spectrum
Hugo A. Camargo, Viktor Jahnke, Keun-Young Kim, and Mitsuhiro Nishida
Journal of High Energy Physics 05 (2023) 226.
Journal · arXiv · PDF
This work investigates Krylov complexity and operator growth in free and interacting massive scalar field theories. We analyze how mass, perturbative interactions, and ultraviolet cutoffs affect the Lanczos coefficients and the growth of Krylov complexity.


Scrambling in hyperbolic black holes: shock waves and pole-skipping
Yongjun Ahn, Viktor Jahnke, Hyun-Sik Jeong, and Keun-Young Kim
Journal of High Energy Physics 10 (2019) 257.
Journal · arXiv · PDF
This work studies information scrambling in hyperbolic black holes using out-of-time-order correlators, gravitational shock waves, and pole-skipping. We show that the shock-wave and pole-skipping approaches yield the same butterfly velocity.


On the chaos bound in rotating black holes
Viktor Jahnke, Keun-Young Kim, and Junggi Yoon
Journal of High Energy Physics 05 (2019) 037.
Journal · arXiv · PDF
This work investigates quantum chaos in rotating BTZ black holes. We show that their out-of-time-order correlators contain left- and right-moving contributions with different Lyapunov exponents and explain how the result remains consistent with the chaos bound when the corresponding effective temperatures are taken into account.


Spectral and Krylov complexity in billiard systems
Hugo A. Camargo, Viktor Jahnke, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim, and Mitsuhiro Nishida
Physical Review D 109, 046017 (2024).
Journal · arXiv · PDF
This work compares spectral and Krylov complexity in integrable circular billiards and chaotic stadium billiards. We identify features of their saturation behavior and Lanczos coefficients that can be used to distinguish integrable from chaotic dynamics.


Pole-skipping of scalar and vector fields in hyperbolic space: conformal blocks and holography
Yongjun Ahn, Viktor Jahnke, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim, Kyung-Sun Lee, and Mitsuhiro Nishida
Journal of High Energy Physics 09 (2020) 111.
Journal · arXiv · PDF
This work derives the pole-skipping points of scalar and vector thermal correlators using both field-theoretic and holographic methods. We relate the leading pole-skipping points to the late-time behavior of conformal blocks in out-of-time-order correlators.


Spread and spectral complexity in quantum spin chains: from integrability to chaos
Hugo A. Camargo, Kyoung-Bum Huh, Viktor Jahnke, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim, and Mitsuhiro Nishida
Journal of High Energy Physics 08 (2024) 241.
Journal · arXiv · PDF
This work investigates spread and spectral complexity across the transition from integrability to chaos in quantum spin chains. We study the mixed-field Ising model and a next-to-nearest-neighbor deformation of the Heisenberg XXZ chain, showing that the characteristic peak of spread complexity provides a signature of chaotic dynamics. We also identify the spectral properties governing the saturation value and timescale of spectral complexity and discuss why the thermofield double state is particularly suitable for probing quantum chaos.

title: Research
text:
My research lies at the interface between quantum chaos and the AdS/CFT correspondence.
The AdS/CFT correspondence provides a framework for studying quantum gravity. It states that certain strongly interacting quantum field theories have an equivalent description in terms of a gravitational theory in an anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. This duality allows questions about quantum gravity to be investigated using the corresponding quantum field theory.
Under generic conditions, strongly interacting and non-integrable quantum systems are expected to display quantum-chaotic behavior. Although the microscopic dynamics of such systems can be extremely complicated, quantum chaos gives rise to universal features, including characteristic energy-level statistics, thermalization, information scrambling, and operator growth.
According to the AdS/CFT correspondence, these universal features must also be reproduced by the dual gravitational theory in AdS. My research uses quantum chaos as a tool to constrain gravitational dynamics and to better understand the inner workings of quantum gravity and black holes.

title: Viktor Jahnke
text:
Theoretical physicist working at the interface between quantum chaos and the AdS/CFT correspondence.
I am a researcher at IFT-UNESP in São Paulo, Brazil.
My research focuses on universal aspects of quantum dynamics and quantum gravity, combining ideas from holography, quantum information, random matrix theory and free probability.
